 1          Pursuant to Civil Local Rule 7-3(d)(1), Plaintiffs object to the new reply evidence submitted with
 2   Defendants Microsoft Corporation and Mojang AB’s Reply in Support of Motion to Compel Arbitration
 3   and Stay Litigation. Specifically, Plaintiffs object to paragraph 3 of the Second Declaration of Michael
 4   Scari, filed as Dkt. 30-1, and to Defendants’ reliance on that paragraph to argue that A.D. continued
 5   using Minecraft, accessed the Minecraft account at issue, accepted the Microsoft Services Agreement, or
 6   manifested an intent not to disaffirm after the May 11, 2026 disaffirmance.
 7          Civil Local Rule 7-3(d)(1) permits an objection to new evidence submitted with a reply, but does
 8   not permit further argument on the motion. Plaintiffs therefore limit this filing to objections to the new
 9   reply evidence and, if the Court is inclined to consider that new evidence, request that the Court consider
10   the limited Supplemental Declaration of Alyce Itsuye Dart submitted solely to address the new May 16,
11   2026 account-access assertion.
12     I.   THE SECOND SCARI DECLARATION PRESENTS NEW REPLY EVIDENCE
13          Plaintiffs object to paragraph 3 of the Second Scari Declaration because it presents new evidence
14   submitted for the first time with Defendants’ reply. Paragraph 3 states: “The Microsoft account
15   registered under Plaintiff Alyce Dart’s email address was accessed as recently as May 16, 2026.”
16   Defendants use this new assertion to argue that “A.D. has subsequently manifested her intent not to
17   disaffirm by continuing to use the Microsoft account after the supposed disaffirmance,” and that A.D.
18   “continued to use the Microsoft account” after May 11, 2026.
19          This evidence was not submitted with Defendants’ opening motion. It also concerns a purported
20   account-access event that allegedly occurred after Plaintiffs filed their opposition and after Ms. Dart’s
21   May 11, 2026 disaffirmance on behalf of A.D. Plaintiffs therefore had no opportunity to address this
22   evidence in their opposition.
23    II.   PARAGRAPH 3 LACKS FOUNDATION FOR DEFENDANTS’ INFERENCE THAT
24          A.D. USED MINECRAFT AFTER DISAFFIRMANCE
25          Plaintiffs object to paragraph 3 of the Second Scari Declaration under Federal Rules of Evidence
26   401, 402, 403, and 602 because the declaration lacks foundation for the inference Defendants ask the
27   Court to draw.
28          Paragraph 3 states only that a “Microsoft account registered under Plaintiff Alyce Dart’s email

18   or around May 16, 2026, using her own device, to use Microsoft Word/Office and print documents.
19   Supp. Dart Decl. ¶¶ 3-6. That access was completely unrelated to Minecraft, was not done on A.D.’s
20   iPad, and was not for the purpose of allowing A.D. to use, access, log into, or play Minecraft. Id. ¶¶ 5-7.
21   Ms. Dart further explains that the Microsoft account associated with her email address is used by her for

 1                                             INTRODUCTION

 2           The claims of Gavin Hays, Alyce Itsuye Dart, and A.D. should be compelled to arbitration.

 3   These plaintiffs do not dispute that they created the Microsoft accounts identified by their counsel.

 4   They also do not dispute that signing up for a Microsoft account requires users to “agree to the

 5   Microsoft Services Agreement” (“MSA”), which includes an arbitration provision. Instead, two

 6   plaintiffs (Mr. Hays and Ms. Dart) argue that they do not need to arbitrate because Microsoft and

 7   Mojang did not produce the exact screens they saw when signing up, because they purportedly do

 8   not remember agreeing to arbitrate, and because they purportedly did not intend to agree to

 9   arbitrate. Yet courts in the Ninth Circuit consistently have held that exemplar screenshots establish
10   an agreement to arbitrate and that lack of recollection and intent do not defeat the formation of an
11   agreement. A third plaintiff (A.D.) attempted to disaffirm the MSA the same day that plaintiffs
12   filed their opposition. But California’s statutory right of disaffirmance for minor contracts does
13   not apply where, as here, a parent entered into a contract on her minor child’s behalf. Even if it

20   they purport to waive public injunctive relief in every forum. The arbitration provision does not merely
21   require individual arbitration. It provides that “Class action lawsuits, class-wide arbitrations, private
22   attorney-general actions, requests for public injunctions, and any other proceeding or request for relief
23   where someone acts in a representative capacity aren’t allowed,” and also bars “combining individual
24   proceedings without the consent of all parties.” Scari Decl., Ex. A § 15.
